Both ligands are my own designs at Phi 2.213, so there is nothing to crossover for - this is refinement. The C4 substituent looks saturated: methyl 0.41, cyclopropyl 0.43, methoxy 0.42 are indistinguishable, and methoxy matching methyl rules out an electronic explanation, so C4 simply wants something compact and I will not gain more by swapping it again. The cap is activity-neutral across cyclopropyl, cyclobutyl and cyclopentyl. That leaves two untried levers: a second substituent on the pyridine, and substitution on the central benzene. This episode takes the first. Atom 0 is the methoxy methyl and the 0-1 bond is acyclic, so anchoring there keeps just that carbon and discards the other 20 atoms; attaching the fragment through a pyridine C4 makes the surviving methyl the 4-methyl, and the fragment carries an additional methyl at C3 plus the whole anilide and cyclopropyl cap. Expected product: 3,4-dimethyl on the pyridine, N-{4-[(3,4-dimethylpyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide at about 267 Da. C3 is adjacent to both the 4-substituent and the bridging NH, so if there is any room left next to the hinge nitrogen this will find it.
